You will serve as a Sea-Launched Cruise Missile (Nuclear) (SLCM-N) Program Analyst at Strategic Systems Program (SSP) in Washington, DC.
You will provide special technical analysis and guidance on procurement, budget execution, and the strategy and planning for SSP.
You will support the SP leadership to integrate SLCM-N acquisition with the development and maintenance of technical documentation, technical design, prototype, and development of the required documents in support of acquisition reviews.
You will support the development of the overall SSP test strategy, technical data package reviews, weapon system analysis, subsystem objective and quality evidence.
You will support the development of integrated master schedules, action plans, and inchstones used to ensure technical rigor is maintained for strategic weapon systems.
Your resume must also demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the NH-03 (GS-13) grade level or pay band in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector.

Specialized experience must demonstrate the following: Provide technical analysis and guidance for major defense systems acquisition to support acquisition planning, budget execution, and lifecycle management in meeting program objectives.

Additional qualification information can be found from the following Office of Personnel Management website:Program Management Series 0340 Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social).

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.

You will. lead complex technology projects by defining requirements, guiding technical decisions, coordinating specialists, and resolving challenges while improving performance, reliability, productivity, and long term planning.
You will evaluate new technologies, recommend system improvements, review proposed solutions, assess technical risks, and support secure, efficient implementations that strengthen organizational operations and future readiness.
You will analyze business needs, design application solutions, oversee development, testing, documentation, and integration, while ensuring software quality, usability, security practices, and dependable performance.
You will develop strategic plans, create and update policies, prepare budgets, measure system performance, conduct program reviews, and recommend improvements that increase effectiveness, efficiency, and service quality.
You will supervise staff by assigning work, setting priorities, evaluating performance, providing coaching, supporting professional development, resolving workplace concerns, and maintaining productive, accountable teams.
You will collaborate with customers, managers, and technical specialists to address project needs, present recommendations, improve organizational processes, and support hiring, training, scheduling, and workforce planning.
Your experience must reflect skill in the following areas: attention to detail, customer service, oral communication, and problem solving. 1. Attention to Detail - Is thorough when performing work and conscientious about attending to detail.

IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: Utilize analytical skills, evaluation techniques, and re-engineering methods to assess the technical, financial, and programmatic implications of prospective IT endeavors. 2.

Customer Service - Works with clients and customers (that is, any individuals who use or receive the services or products that your work unit produces, including the general public, individuals who work in the agency, other agencies, or organizations outside the Government) to assess their needs, provide information or assistance, resolve their problems, or satisfy their expectations; knows about available products and services; is committed to providing quality products and services.

IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: Manage stakeholder requirements from internal/external agencies helping execute and accomplish organizational goals and objectives. 3.

Oral Communication - Expresses information (for example, ideas or facts) to individuals or groups effectively, taking into account the audience and nature of the information (for example, technical, sensitive, controversial); makes clear and convincing oral presentations; listens to others, attends to nonverbal cues, and responds appropriately.

IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: Providing leadership, guidance, and mentorship to the workforce communicating organizational goals and objectives while aligning with the command's initiatives. 4.

Problem Solving - Identifies problems; determines accuracy and relevance of information; uses sound judgment to generate and evaluate alternatives, and to make recommendations. IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: analysis, reporting, coordinating, and facilitating working groups to meet and resolve project objectives.

In addition: Your resume must also demonstrate at least one year of Specialized experience at or equivalent to the GS-13 grade level or NH-03 pay band in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector. Specialized experience must demonstrate the following: 1.

Ability to effectively manage and supervise a staff of professional, technical, and/or administrative employees. 2. Mastery knowledge of and demonstrated experience in applying Information Technology principles and practices. 3. Ability to supervise and work on a diverse team engaged in Defense Acquisition program management activities. 4.

Mastery knowledge of current/emerging Congressional, regulatory, and higher headquarters directives and guidance. 5.

Mastery knowledge of any of the following functional areas: - Application Software - Customer Support - Data Management - Internet - Network Services - Operating Systems - Policy and Planning - Security - Systems Administration - Systems Analysis 6. Ability to communicate effectively both orally and in writing.

Hi, I'm Jace , and I founded Ashby's Customer Education function in 2025. We've expanded the team since then, I now lead the team and am excited to be hiring our next Program Manager!
Our team is built on a simple belief: Ashby Academy should feel like every customer's personal CSM. Regardless of tier or team size, every Ashby customer deserves content that meets them where they are — practical, accurate, and genuinely useful.

That standard shapes everything we build, and it's what's driven the development of our growing Academy courses, webinar program, and playbook library. We have ambitions to expand both the depth of our content and the formats we deliver it in, and this hire is a meaningful part of getting there.
As our next Customer Education Program Manager, you'll own customer-facing education work end to end. We're looking for someone who knows Ashby well enough to coach users on how to use it, and can translate that coaching into content that scales. You'll turn complex product workflows into clear, practical learning experiences, and partner closely with Customer Success, Product, PMM, and Recruiting Operations Consulting to make sure what we build is grounded in how customers actually work.
This is a hands-on role. You won't be setting strategy and handing it off. You'll be in the work: scoping, writing, building, reviewing, refining, and shipping.

Own net-new customer education work from concept through publication, including courses, playbooks, recordings, and other learning assets
Define the goal and shape of each learning asset — what it should help customers do, for whom, and in what format — then gather SME input, design the approach, and build it
Refresh and improve existing Academy content so it stays aligned with how Ashby actually works today
Translate complex Ashby workflows into clear, practical, outcome-oriented education — the kind that helps customers understand not just what to do, but why it matters
Partner cross-functionally with CS, Product, PMM, and RecOps Consultants to identify high-value education opportunities and get the right assets out at the right time
Contribute to the systems, standards, and workflows that help Customer Education scale while maintaining high-quality learning experiences
Help us explore adjacent formats when useful — lighter-weight tutorials, in-app guidance, and other just-in-time learning moments
Typical workload: You'll manage 2-3 new courses or major playbooks per quarter, plus ongoing refreshes and maintenance of existing content. Most of your time goes into building the work yourself (writing, recording, designing learning flows).
Examples of work you might own
Build a new Academy course that helps customers adopt a new Ashby feature or module
Turn product and SME input into a practical playbook tied to a real recruiting outcome
Record voiceover for a customer-facing learning asset
Audit and refresh an existing course after a product change so it reflects how Ashby works today
Partner with RecOps Consulting or other SMEs to build something that helps customers apply a concept, not just understand it
Experiment with lighter-weight format when a full course isn't the right answer

You already know Ashby well. You understand how its workflows are structured, where users can get stuck, and what it takes to use it effectively. Formal customer education experience isn't required. What matters is Ashby fluency and the ability to translate that into coaching and content.
Beyond your Ashby depth, you could be a great fit if you also have:
You've taught something complex before. Whether live, through writing, or both, you've helped someone understand a complicated product or process and have ideas on how to turn that into something scalable.
You can juggle multiple projects. You manage several at once without losing momentum when priorities shift.
You're a strong writer. You can make complicated things feel clear and useful on the page.
You're comfortable recording voiceovers. Recording yourself for customer-facing content feels natural, not like a stretch.
You own work end-to-end. You can take something from problem framing through build and launch without needing a fully mapped plan first.
You work well with subject matter experts. You know how to pull what you need from busy stakeholders without losing momentum or clarity.
You have good judgment about scope. You can tell when something should be deep, lightweight, or optimized for speed, and you choose intentionally.
Traditional customer education experience isn't required. The background that matters most is hands-on Ashby experience — as a recruiter, a recruiting ops practitioner, an implementation specialist, a CSM, or someone who has simply used Ashby deeply enough to teach it. If you've owned meaningful work with real autonomy, improved how something gets taught or documented, and cared about outcomes over optics, you'll likely feel at home here.
This role may not be a fit if
You're still building Ashby fluency. This role leans on already knowing Ashby well, since you'll be teaching it from day one. If you haven't had the chance to build that hands-on depth yet, this particular role isn't the right fit.
You prefer to set strategy and hand it off. This is a hands-on role. You'll be the one scoping, writing, recording, and shipping, not directing someone else to do it.
You need a fully defined scope before you can do your best work. You'll often be the one deciding what shape an asset takes and how deep to take it, without a fully mapped plan.
You'd rather optimize an established system than help shape one. You'll have the chance to define how this program works and put your stamp on the approach, building something you're proud of rather than fine-tuning what's already set.
You want a coordination or project-management role. This is a maker seat. Most of your time goes into building the work yourself, not managing a queue of other people's.
You measure success by how much content ships. We care about whether the right education gets built and whether customers actually use it: engagement, progress, adoption of the workflows it supports, and reduced dependence on 1:1 support are all signs that the work is landing.
You're energized by large, highly structured teams. You'll often be responsible for identifying where structure is needed and putting it in place yourself
About Ashby
We’re building the next generation of enterprise software and we’re starting with a suite of products that help talent leaders, recruiters, and hiring managers run their hiring process significantly better. We are well-funded, have incredible product market fit, and are backed by great investors, including Y Combinator, Elad Gil and Lachy Groom
We have notable customers like Notion, Linear, Shopify, and Snowflake. Our growth and retention metrics are best-in-class among our peers: we have tens of millions in ARR, growing >100% year over year, over 4,000 customers, very low churn, and many years of runway. We’ll share more details once we meet, but you now probably have a good idea as to why we're hiring for this role

You will serve as a Technical Project Lead (TPL) for the Afloat Counter Unmanned Systems (ACUS) portfolio.
You will be responsible for the technical baseline and risk management, employing an agile, iterative approach to evaluate emerging technologies and ensure the continuous delivery of safe, authorized, and effective C-UxS solutions.
You will lead technical efforts by coordinating activities across Ship Integration and Certification, Launcher and Gun-Based Effectors, Fire Direction, and Systems Engineering.
You will provide hands-on guidance to a diverse engineering team, ensuring strict adherence to engineering best practices and driving the technical review of all deliverables.
You will lead a cross-functional team to ensure successful project execution and alignment with program and sponsor goals, while fostering collaboration across technical and programmatic disciplines to achieve project success.
You will evaluate emerging technologies and systems to accelerate delivery of rapid capabilities to the Fleet, employing a highly agile, iterative engineering approach focused on continuous/rapid deployment of effective ship self-defense solutions.
You will provide hands-on technical leadership to a diverse engineering team, resolving complex system issues, enforcing engineering best practices, and validating all technical deliverables prior to fleet release.
You will serve as the primary technical engineering authority, owning the engineering approach, driving key design decisions, and actively managing technical risks to ensure system viability.
You will formulate strategic technical guidance and roadmaps in collaboration with the ACUS leadership team to ensure project activities integrate seamlessly into the overall program strategy and support the long-term viability of C-UxS capabilities.
You will lead the technical execution and delivery of project products to the Fleet, interfacing directly with program offices, In­Service Engineering Agents (ISEA), and stakeholders to ensure seamless integration.
You will manage, execute, and report on project operations, serving as the first line of escalation for project-specific successes and challenges, and collaborating closely with program leadership to address and resolve issues.
You will execute rigorous administrative project management duties, including developing Statements of Work (SOW), spend plans, and ensuring compliance with NSWCDD, E Department, Division, and Afloat Counter Unmanned Systems (ACUS) policies.
You will serve as the primary project representative, communicating effectively with team members, sponsors, and external organizations (as delegated by the PM) to ensure complete transparency and alignment with overarching program goals.
Your resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the ND-04 (GS-12/13 equivalent) pay band in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector as a professional engineer or scientist leading the technical architecture, design, and systems engineering of Department of War weapon systems.

Examples of qualifying experience may include: (1) Serving as a technical authority or lead systems engineer, owning the technical approach and making key engineering design decisions for complex weapon systems, effectors, or fire direction systems; (2) Providing hands-on technical leadership to engineering teams, including the review and validation of technical deliverables, the execution of formal systems engineering processes, and the active management of technical risks; (3) Leading technical efforts in design, development and integration of emerging capabilities.

Additional qualification information can be found from the following Office of Personnel Management website: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/#url=List-by-Occupational-Series AND https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/0800/files/all-professional-engineering-positions-0800.pdf General Physical Science Series, 1301 (opm.gov) Operations Research Series 1515 (opm.gov) Mathematics Series 1520 (opm.gov) Computer Science Series 1550 (opm.gov) Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social).

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.

Prior experience managing contracts with multiple interdependent CLINs under a T&M ceiling structure. Background Requirements: Must possess or be eligible to obtain and complete a Public Trust background investigation and/or a Public Trust clearance. Citizenship Status Required: Must be a U.S.

About InAir
InAir is a forward-thinking, fully remote consulting firm with a stronghold in Texas. We are proud experts in Airtable consulting services, partnering with mid-sized to large enterprises. Our mission is to harness the power of low-code platforms, enabling businesses to optimize their workflows, foster collaboration, and achieve ambitious outcomes through Airtable.
At our company, we foster a culture of honesty, responsibility, and accountability. These core values create a successful, innovative, and transparent workplace. Our remote work setting is built on trust, respect, and open communication, allowing team members to shine and grow.

We're looking for a Technical Project Manager to own client projects from first discovery call to final delivery — with a twist: this is a hands-on role. You won't just manage the work; you'll build a significant part of it yourself in Airtable.
Think of it as the intersection of three skills: understanding how a business operates, managing a project to done, and configuring the system with your own hands. If you've ever been the person at your company who "figured out the tools" and ended up running the whole process, this role was built for you.
A dedicated Engineer covers custom code — you cover everything else: the client, the plan, and the build.

Own the client: Be the primary point of contact for a portfolio of enterprise clients. Lead discovery, manage expectations, and turn business goals into concrete requirements.
Run the project: Own scope, priorities, and timelines. Coordinate day-to-day execution with our Engineer and keep momentum consistent across accounts.
Build in Airtable: Configure tables, automations, and interfaces yourself. You're not writing code, but you are building the system.
Make systems better: Review existing client implementations and improve their structure, usability, and scalability.

Project leadership with your hands in the work. Experience running client-facing or cross-functional projects where you also built or configured the solution — not just tracked tickets.
A power-user profile. You've mastered tools like Airtable, Notion, Asana, HubSpot, Zapier, or similar — deeply enough to design processes in them, not just use them.
Comfort with structured data. You get how tables relate to each other and why clean structure keeps a growing system from breaking. Formal database training is a plus rather than a prerequisite.
Strong communication. You can lead a meeting with executives and translate between business and technical worlds.
Accountability. You own outcomes across multiple projects at once and don't wait to be told what's next.

Airtable experience (a big plus — but we'll train the right builder).
Background in consulting, agencies, RevOps, or operations.
Familiarity with the low-code/no-code ecosystem.
Experience with ClickUp.
Structure & Availability
Full-time (40 hours/week), fully remote. This is a core client-facing role: you'll need stable, dedicated availability aligned with US business hours.

You are the central interface between Engineering and Product Management. Product owns product strategy, prioritization, and requirements; together with the Development Leads, you ensure these are translated into technically sound, realistically planned, and reliably delivered solutions.
This is not a traditional IT project management role: you bring a strong technical background yourself and can make architecture and design decisions together with our Development Leads, assess technical risks, and evaluate different solution approaches.
Alongside short-term delivery, you also keep long-term technical topics in view, including architecture, maintainability, security, technical debt, and the continuous improvement of our engineering standards.
You actively drive our AI First Development Culture. Your profile You have at least 5 years of relevant professional experience in or around software development and have worked hands-on as a software developer yourself.
You bring proven experience leading developers and development teams and have already held both functional and disciplinary leadership responsibility.
You have experience managing software development projects: you have coordinated multiple developers and stakeholders, owned planning and timelines, managed dependencies, and guided releases through to delivery.
You are technically deep enough to understand and shape architecture decisions, identify technical risks early, and discuss technical topics with experienced developers at eye level.

You communicate clearly and convincingly and are equally comfortable coordinating with Engineering, Product Management, and senior management.
You bring a collaborative leadership style, strong organizational skills, and a genuine desire to shape and improve how we work.

The Arctic is a place of extremes: unforgiving, untamed, and undergoing rapid change. A literal defrosting reveals a multi-trillion-dollar opportunity spanning energy, defence, logistics, research, and infrastructure.
ARD was founded on a paradox. The Arctic is both the next great economic frontier and one of the most hostile environments on Earth. Rich in resources and strategically vital, yet bone-chillingly cold, dark for months, and fundamentally inhospitable to humans. This paradox - an explosion of activity in a place that resists human presence - is why we exist. Our solution is autonomy.
We build systems that operate reliably and intelligently in the Arctic, so that humans don't always have to.
Founded by record-holding pioneers with decades of polar experience, we take calculated risks on hard problems that matter. If you want to build and deploy ground-up technology with real-world impact, at an inflection point in history that won’t reappear, we’d like to talk.

Our engineering team is expanding rapidly, and we’re looking for a Technical Project Manager to sit at the heart of it, driving delivery across our engineering portfolio. This is a hands-on role for someone who thrives on ambiguity, moves fast, and can bring order to multiple complex, multi-disciplinary hardware projects without slowing them down.
You'll be responsible for planning, tracking, and de-risking delivery across products at varying stages of maturity - from early-TRL prototypes through to fielded, mission-ready systems - and from field-ready energy systems to autonomous surface and sub-surface platforms.

Own project planning and delivery tracking across concurrent engineering projects and work streams (firmware, electronics, mechanical, testing), translating product strategy and portfolio priorities into executable projects with clear milestones, owners, and outcomes.
Convert ambitious commercial and operational deadlines into realistic, resourced delivery plans — holding the line on both ambition and delivery discipline.
Maintain visibility across work streams, dependencies, risks, decisions, and resourcing gaps, managing technical risk and dependency mapping across products at different Technology Readiness Levels (TRL) and adjusting project rigour and testing requirements accordingly.
Take ownership of BOMs for any existing and future products, manage key supplier relationships and keep track of all materials deliveries.
Technical Expertise: Understand the architecture, dependencies, and technical challenges of hardware design and development. Support engineering teams in resolving technical issues. Ensure compliance with industry standards and government regulations, such as MIL-STD, UK DEFSTAN, and STANAG testing and qualification requirements across the product lifecycle.
Act as the connective tissue across engineering, procurement, business development, security, product, commercial, and customers — driving cross-functional alignment and ensuring technical progress, customer commitments, and delivery constraints are understood on all sides.
Identify and resolve blockers fast, escalate early and clearly, and provide concise, decision-ready updates on consequential tradeoffs.
Build and refine the project management tooling, processes, and reporting cadence as ARD scales — you'll be creating much of this from scratch.
Identify missing handoffs and unwritten work, converting them into accountable plans, and facilitate requirements and scope definition with product, customer, and technical owners.
Lead pilots, implementations, migrations, rollouts, adoption, and operational handoffs.

The Aviation Regulatory Project Manager performs multiple, varying, and highly complex assignments under minimal direction from a manager or senior leader.

Serves as a principal technical specialist and project manager for major regulatory, operational, and integration activities involving Unmanned Aircraft Systems, Unmanned Aircraft Traffic Management, and Advanced Air Mobility for ensuring safe and effective integration into the National Airspace System (NAS).

Applies experience and comprehensive technical knowledge of emerging aviation operations, operational practices, and regulatory requirements to conduct both regulatory and operational evaluations to support the safe integration of emerging aviation operations into the NAS.

Conducts regulatory evaluations by interpreting and assessing the applicability of existing regulations, identifying compliance requirements, and determining where emerging operational models or technologies create gaps, conflicts, or misalignments with current regulatory frameworks.

Performs operational evaluations by analyzing procedures, system interactions, workflow impacts, and safety considerations to determine how emerging aviation operations function within the NAS and to identify operational risks or procedural inconsistencies requiring mitigation.

Integrates the results of both regulatory and operational evaluations to develop technical recommendations, support rule-making activities, and inform updates to operational criteria and compliance guidance.

Possesses an understanding of new technologies and methodologies, to solve complex problems and develop improved technical processes or systems. Conducts extensive research and analysis to evaluate how new operational models, technologies, or procedures align with existing regulatory requirements.

Integrates analytical results into project deliverables that support rule-making activities, regulatory evaluations, and updates to operational criteria. Evaluates complex operational scenarios to identify gaps, conflicts, or inconsistencies in regulatory applicability, compliance requirements, or operational procedures.

Performs root-cause analysis of operational or compliance issues involving emerging aviation operations and prepares technical findings that inform regulatory updates or operational mitigations.

Uses project management principles to plan, coordinate, and execute complex regulatory and operational evaluation activities and projects involving emerging aviation operations.

Develops project plans, schedules, and milestones to guide the assessment of operational data, procedures, and system interactions; and identifies safety risks, compliance concerns, and regulatory inconsistencies requiring higher-level analysis.

Ensures that project deliverables, analytical findings, and technical recommendations meet regulatory requirements, adhere to project objectives, and align with the priorities of the major subdivision and broader organizational goals.

Monitors project progress, identifies risks or delays, and implements corrective actions to maintain schedule and quality. Tracks project performance metrics; and prepares comprehensive regulatory analyses, compliance assessments, technical reports, and operational findings as key project outputs.

Consolidates operational, regulatory, and technical information into products that support decision-making and operational integration activities. Defines, organizes, and assigns resources to accomplish large regulatory, operational, and analytical work activities. Allocates resources to accomplish large work activities within established schedules.

Works across organizational boundaries to complete complex evaluations, research activities, and support tasks within established schedules. Provides policy guidance and instruction to others, both internally and externally.

Specialized experience is experience that has equipped you with the particular knowledge, skills, and abilities to perform successfully the duties of the position.

Specialized Experience: Experience researching and interpreting operational and regulatory information to contribute to the preparation of analytical summaries, findings, or recommendations.

Experience analyzing operational data, procedures, and technical information to identify trends, assess impacts, and support regulatory or operational evaluations. Applicants should include examples of specialized experience in their work history.
